long_biography.plain_text:
Oracle's early advantage came from Larry Ellison's decision to commercialise relational-database research before IBM brought its own work to market. He and his partners built a system for the CIA, then adapted the technology for business customers under the Oracle name.

A severe reversal in 1990 tested Ellison's control of the company. After rapid growth gave way to losses and a collapsing valuation, he replaced much of the senior management and concentrated on product development. Oracle 7 restored the database business to leadership, and Ellison later expanded the company through acquisitions before directing its shift towards cloud infrastructure and artificial intelligence.
